title: Latency-bounded Reservation Allocator and Incremental Utilization Reporter
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce a latency-bounded reservation allocator that ensures per-request tail-latency SLOs while making soft capacity reservations; add an incremental utilization reporter that streams summarized per-pool utilization metrics for efficient storage and real-time dashboards.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need predictable tail latency for tenant requests while still allowing short bursts and efficient packing. Existing reservoir-style allocators optimize for long-term fairness but do not provide explicit bounds for p95/p99 tail latency during transient bursts. This change introduces a reservation allocator that trades small, short-lived soft reservations to keep queueing latency under explicit bounds and a companion incremental utilization reporter that emits compact deltas suitable for high-cardinality fleets.

Summary of changes: implement a latency-bounded reservation allocator in the autoscaler which: 1) continuously estimates per-pool service capacity and current queueing headroom; 2) creates short-duration soft reservations (configurable TTL and decay curves) when queueing delay prediction exceeds configured latency SLO; 3) honors proportional tenant shares to avoid long-term unfairness; 4) exposes decision diagnostics for tracing and debugging. Add a util reporter process that: 1) aggregates utilization at multiple timescales (10s/1m/5m) and emits incremental deltas rather than full snapshots to reduce ingestion costs; 2) tags records with origin (autoscaler vs. gateway) and reservation attribution; 3) surfaces percentiles and decay-weighted averages used by the allocator.

Design notes: the allocator is conservative by default (defaults tuned in charts/dedicated/values.yaml) and has three knobs: latency_slo_ms, reservation_ttl_s, and reservation_decay_factor. Reservation_credit accounting is soft—credits can be reclaimed early if headroom returns. The util reporter uses a windowed sampler with an exponentially weighted delta compressor; it includes backpressure when the telemetry pipeline is saturated.

Compatibility and rollout: implemented feature-flagging for both allocator and reporter. Default: disabled in hosted by default; enabled on Dedicated environments behind an opt-in config. Rollout plan includes canary in one pool, monitor p95/p99 latency, utilization deltas, and tenant throughput impact. Rollback: disable feature flag and drain outstanding soft reservations (immediate reclamation path included).

Testing: unit tests cover allocator decision logic and invariants (no negative credits, proportional fairness over 10k simulated ticks). Integration tests simulate bursty traffic across tenants and assert p95/p99 under configured SLOs. Bench harness included to measure CPU and memory of the reporter under 100k series.

Checklist: - [x] Implement allocator logic and unit tests - [x] Implement incremental util reporter and unit tests - [x] Add integration tests and smoke harness - [x] Add docs/design/reservation-allocator.md - [x] Add Helm defaults and migration notes - [x] Manual canary run and metrics validation

Related: ENG-9742 (autoscaler backpressure refactor), ENG-9801 (telemetry cost-reduction initiative).

notes_for_ops: If you enable allocator in production, start with conservative latency_slo_ms (e.g., 250ms) and low reservation_ttl_s (e.g., 5s). Monitor auto-reservation rate and telemetry queue backlog metric 'telemetry.delta_backpressure'. If backlog grows, temporarily disable reporter or increase telemetry ingress capacity.
